summary.value: The Dampierre is a young French breed made in 1996 by fanciers who wanted to bring back the Normande, an old Normandy chicken that had died out more than a hundred years before. They could not revive the exact bird, so they built a close likeness from Gournay and Crevecoeur stock. The result is mottled black and white like the Gournay and wears a feather crest on its head. It is a dual purpose bird, with fine white meat on light bones. Hens lay a good number of large white eggs and will go broody and sit on a clutch. The breed is still very rare, especially outside France, and published details on its weight, laying totals and temperament are hard to find. It suits keepers who enjoy uncommon heritage style birds.
